_comment: Manually verified service terms missing from every automated source (openstates people files, docs.legis listings, legacy CSV). Each entry cites its basis. Never inferred. An entry with "exclusive": true declares the complete verified service for that person+chamber: the importer then skips roster supplements for that chamber, so any service the curation misses fails the vote-coverage gate loudly.

ocd-person/82c2d686-98d3-4dc9-8655-4e610.basis: Jerry Petrowski represented AD 86 until winning the SD 29 special election of June 5, 2012 (vacancy from Pam Galloway's resignation); the legacy CSV records his whole 2011-2012 term as Senate only.

Petrowski assumed the SD 29 seat on July 17, 2012 (Ballotpedia; special election of June 5, 2012). Ends at the biennium boundary where roster supplements take over; blocks the phantom Jan 2011-Jul 2012 Senate coverage the legacy CSV implied.

ocd-person/7da63875-0a3c-4b03-aaa8-fe48c.basis: Marker only: Jill Billings' real Assembly term (AD 95 from Jan 26, 2012, per her openstates file and Ballotpedia) is her complete service. The openstates legacy CSV wrongly credits her legacy id WIL000419 with the 2009-2010 AD 95 seat, which was Jennifer Shilling's; without this marker that row earns her a phantom 2009-2010 supplement.

ocd-person/2e0e6bb3-bb92-4b34-90bc-a22ff.basis: Caleb Frostman's complete Senate service: sworn in June 28, 2018 after winning the June 12 special election (vacancy from Frank Lasee's resignation), served until Jan 7, 2019 after losing the November 2018 general. His openstates role is startless, and the one-constitutional-term guess would fabricate 2015-2018 presence.

ocd-person/5e70f623-ae29-4013-ac58-b86c2.basis: Peter Barca was sworn into the 2019 Assembly on Jan 7, took the oath as Revenue Secretary the same day, and resigned the seat (in office at DOR from Jan 8, 2019 per WisPolitics/Wikipedia). This one-day term blocks the whole-biennium 2019 supplement his startless role would otherwise earn.

ocd-person/798979da-9683-41b4-b663-d5c73.basis: Dora Drake assumed the SD 4 seat on Dec 19, 2024 (Ballotpedia; July 30, 2024 special election for Lena Taylor's vacancy). Adjacent to her regular-term start Jan 6, 2025; blocks the phantom Jan 2023-Dec 2024 Senate coverage a 2023-session supplement would grant.

ocd-person/e127b754-c756-4017-a414-83cff.basis: Joel Kitchens was sworn in Jan 5, 2015 (Assembly Journal opening day; he appears on the AR1/AR2/SJR1 roll calls of that date); the openstates start 2015-01-06 is a day late. Bridge term covers the verified first day.

ocd-person/2a067a93-dffc-4ce7-8975-d37fb.basis: David Steffen was sworn in Jan 5, 2015 (Assembly Journal opening day; he appears on the AR1/AR2/SJR1 roll calls of that date); the openstates start 2015-01-06 is a day late. Bridge term covers the verified first day.

ocd-person/eed49381-7c5b-4890-bba3-d63b8.basis: Lisa Subeck was sworn in Jan 5, 2015 (Assembly Journal opening day; she appears on the AR1/AR2/SJR1 roll calls of that date); the openstates start 2015-01-07 is two days late. Bridge term covers the verified first days.

ocd-person/2a532097-b605-4d3e-90ce-d8ae3.basis: Jennifer Shilling represented AD 95 until winning the SD 32 recall election of August 9, 2011 (defeating Dan Kapanke); she took the Senate seat on Aug 26, 2011. The legacy CSV records her whole 2011-2012 term as Senate only.

Shilling took the SD 32 seat on Aug 26, 2011 after the recall win (Ballotpedia). Ends at the biennium boundary where roster supplements take over; blocks the phantom Jan-Aug 2011 Senate coverage the legacy CSV implied.

ocd-person/34a948bb-7d10-442e-97d5-dae4b.basis: John Lehman was sworn into the SD 21 seat on July 16, 2012 after winning the June 5, 2012 recall against Van Wanggaard (Ballotpedia). Ends at the biennium boundary where roster supplements take over; blocks the phantom Jan 2011-Jul 2012 Senate coverage.
